observationsNotFindings: The best thing in this artifact is a citation it declines to make. Six sibling gate joins in this sweep ground their standing on their harness's leftoverNameNote, and the obvious way to write this one would have been to reuse that sentence. G09 v3 has no such field - zero occurrences, no key at any depth - and the artifact says so explicitly in five places while grounding itself on leftoverDesignClosedIfAcceptedAndRecorded, which does exist and names exactly OBL-G09-HARNESS-SPEC. Pattern-following would have produced a fabricated citation that a field-level check would catch only if someone thought to look.

The folding prohibition is enforced structurally rather than by assertion. R-10 and R-6 live in their own field, namedRaceByteSetsNotAuthored, separate from the fourteen FX in namedCorpusNotAuthored, and both match live G09 v3 under ==. A sweep of every FX token returns exactly the fourteen. Keeping two named sets in two fields is harder to get wrong later than keeping them in one with a caveat.

This is the third gate-row and register-row coexistence in the sweep - after G18 with DR-107 and G20 with DR-125 - and the third to show zero divergence on shared obligations. Three clean instances make the pattern look deliberate. The standing caution is unchanged: nothing structural keeps the pairs aligned, so a coordinator recording either member should re-check the agreement.

G09's live assurance cell reads SPECIFIED where every other gate in this sweep reads 'PROPOSED; not QUALIFIED', and the artifact reproduces the difference. Small, but it is the kind of cell a family-pattern author copies without looking.
